_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for BKR retrospectives (retro/build_bkr.py): Baker Hughes Incorporated, listed on the NYSE as BHI throughout 2007-2009 (BKR is the series key). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 were accepted before the open on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), and the latest declared dividend. Fiscal years are calendar years from 1998 (fiscal 1997 ended September 30). Baker Hughes gives no EPS, total-revenue or margin guidance in numbers in any filing of 2007-2009: each release's Outlook section guides revenue outside North America (in words or as a range), corporate expenses, capital expenditures, depreciation and the tax rate, kept on the print as 'outlook' (display only), and the 2009 releases have no Outlook section. Values are as reported; a vintage takes each year from the latest filing that reports it, and the company's operating profit per diluted share replaces GAAP EPS where a filing publishes it (the history's 'normalization' says which). A print's growth rates and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw'; the builder re-derives and checks them): the year-ago quarter is the one the same release shows. Outside North America is the release's Oilfield Operations revenue less North America. rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing. From 2017-07-05 the listed company is Baker Hughes, a GE company (BHGE; Baker Hughes Company, BKR, from October 2019), built as a new listing ('listing'): the entries marked "era": "bhge" (vintages, prints, guides) and 'rule_t_bhge' are that company's and the only ones its models read; nothing of Baker Hughes Incorporated's history, prints or dividends enters them, and nothing of theirs enters a date before the listing. Its statements before July 3, 2017 are GE Oil & Gas's, with no per-share figures; 2017 (a loss for July 3 to December 31) is not a full year, so the first date is the one after the Q4 2018 release. EPS is GAAP diluted income per Class A share: the releases give adjusted EPS by quarter only, no filing gives a full-year figure excluding identified items, and nothing is derived; a year whose identified items attributable to the company exceed its net income ('one_off_test') or that is a loss is excluded. Share counts are Class A plus Class B outstanding at year end. A print's growth rates and margins are derived from its release's raw figures: orders and revenue against the year-ago quarter, the gross margin (revenue less cost of revenue), total segment operating income on revenue and the operating margin. 'listings' holds later changes of symbol and exchange. From 2022 (the two segments of October 2022, then the statement of income of 2025) a print lists its segments under 'segments' and a margin its release does not report is null: total segment operating income is the release's total, or its two segments summed where it gives no total (Q3 and Q4 2024), and is not reported from Q1 2025 (segment EBITDA instead), like operating income. From the Q4 2023 release the company publishes the year's adjusted diluted EPS, which replaces GAAP ('eps_basis'; 2022's, first published there, enters the history through 'restates'). The new company's dividend changes carry "era" in 'dividends'; a guide with 'rev_guide_m' is a fiscal-year revenue guide in dollars.

history_vintages.why: Baker Hughes: 'We are a leading provider of drilling, formation evaluation, completion and production products and services to the worldwide oil and natural gas industry'; 'The primary driver of our business is our customers’ capital and operating expenditures dedicated to exploring, and drilling for, and developing and producing oil and natural gas'; 'Our business is cyclical and is dependent upon our customers’ forecasts of future oil and natural gas prices, future economic growth and hydrocarbon demand and estimates of future oil and natural gas production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed' (its own FY2006 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' drilling and production spending through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oilfield services company
